statement: Define named layers with show/hide, lock, shaded-or-wireframe 3D display, an intersection-group number and an optional name extension, with each element on exactly one layer and an undeletable fallback layer always present.
superiority: Layers are tags with sets and rules, not an exclusive single assignment, while staying import-compatible.

acceptance.sketch: Create 20 layers, hide 3: elements on hidden layers vanish from plan and 3D; count equals filter.

notes: CORRECTED — wireframe is a per-layer 3D display mode, one layer per element, a permanent fallback layer exists, name extension added; read Layers, Layers dialog, Layer status.

statement: Save named layer combinations holding each layer's show/hide, lock and 3D-mode status, apply one to the current view, and store the chosen combination with every view.
superiority: Combinations are diffable and can be derived from queries.

acceptance.sketch: Apply combination: exactly the stored layers visible; view saves its link.

notes: VERIFIED — read Layer Combinations; combinations are edited with an Update step and applied from quick options, layer settings or view settings.

statement: Give each layer an intersection-group number so elements connect at junctions only when their layers share a group, and elements both on group 0 never connect.

source.ref: Layers > Use layers to prevent intersections

superiority: Intersection behavior is stated by relation rather than an obscure number.

acceptance.sketch: Walls on layers in different groups cross without cleanup; same group joins; two walls both on group 0 never join; a hidden same-group layer still joins.

notes: CORRECTED — group 0 never connects, default is group 1, hidden layers still intersect; groups are plain tags, not priorities. Read Use layers to prevent intersections.

statement: Define line types as solid (fixed), dashed (dash and gap lengths) or symbol (stencil of lines, arcs and hotspots), each scaling either with the model or at a fixed paper size.

source.ref: Lines > Edit and manage line types

superiority: Same definitions exportable to DWG linetypes without loss.

acceptance.sketch: Dash pattern 3 mm on 1 mm off prints periodically at 1:50 and 1:100 as set.

notes: CORRECTED — solid is not editable; dashed and symbol editors exist; scale with plan or paper-size. Read Lines, Edit Line Type (Dashed), Edit Line Type (Symbol).

statement: Define fills as vector patterns, solid fills with opacity, symbol fills pasted from 2D elements, or image fills, each with unit size and rotation and a choice of model-scaled or paper-fixed size.
superiority: Fills are resolution-independent and exact on export to vector formats.

acceptance.sketch: A paper-fixed vector fill keeps its defined spacing within 0.01 mm at 1:100 and 1:200; a model-scaled one halves its paper spacing when the scale denominator doubles.

notes: CORRECTED — 'hatch' is not a type; types are vector, solid, symbol, image. Read Fills, Edit Vector Fill, Create/Edit Solid Fill, Create/Edit Symbol Fill, Create Image Fill.

statement: Tag each fill as drafting, cover and/or cut so that fill choosers offer only fills valid for the context: drafting for the fill tool, cover for surfaces and elements, cut for building materials and section cuts.
superiority: Single hierarchy with explicit usage tags.

acceptance.sketch: A fill tagged cover only is absent from the building-material cut-fill chooser and present in the surface cover-fill chooser.

notes: CORRECTED — three availability categories, not just cut versus cover; image fills cannot be cut fills. Read Fill Categories.

statement: Define surfaces for the basic engine with colour, transmittance, emission, cover fill and texture, and separate richer channel settings for the Cineware engine, each engine keeping its own parameters.
superiority: PBR material model mapped from legacy values with round-trip.

acceptance.sketch: Surface with 50 percent transparency renders consistent in 3D view.

notes: CORRECTED — 'glow, specular, bump' belong to Cineware channels; basic engine uses colour, transmittance, attenuation, emission. Read Edit and manage surfaces, Surface Exposure to Light settings, Match surface settings.

statement: Control a surface texture's size, proportion and rotation, and realign texture origin and direction on selected 3D elements, with a reset to per-element-type default alignment.
superiority: Mapping overrides editable in 3D with live preview.

acceptance.sketch: Setting the texture origin at a wall corner starts the brick pattern there on every face; Reset Texture restores alignment parallel to the reference line.

notes: CORRECTED — 'fit to surface/linear' overrides not found; documented are Set Origin, Set Direction, Reset Texture and default alignments. Read Texture settings (Basic Engine), Align 3D Texture, Default Texture Alignments.

statement: Add surfaces to a project from a catalogue of the active libraries or an online component portal, searching library part name, library, description, subtype, author and keywords and showing at most 50 hits.

source.ref: Surfaces > Search for surfaces in catalog

superiority: Cloud-hosted material library with versioning, so every project resolves surfaces by stable IDs.

acceptance.sketch: Import a catalogue of 200 surfaces twice: second import detects duplicates by name and checksum and adds none.

notes: CORRECTED — help documents add-from-catalog, replace-from-catalog and catalog search (50 hit cap); no catalogue-checksum duplicate detection. Read Add new surface from catalog, Search for surfaces in catalog.

statement: Let each building material supply the element's surface, and let any element override the surface per face or edge, optionally linking all faces to one override, with removal restoring the material surface.

source.ref: Surfaces > Override surface in element settings

superiority: Face overrides tracked like attributes.

acceptance.sketch: Face-level override shows in render.

notes: CORRECTED — override is per face/edge with a link toggle; library objects use their own surface parameters. Read Override surface in element settings.

statement: Define building materials combining cut fill with foreground and background pens, fill orientation, surface and intersection priority, plus ID, manufacturer, description and physical data such as conductivity, density, heat capacity, embodied carbon and embodied energy.
superiority: Properties align with IFC material and energy analysis.

acceptance.sketch: Wall quantity: volume * density = mass.

notes: CORRECTED — cost is not a building-material field; embodied carbon and energy are. Read Building Materials, Edit and manage Building Materials, Building Material Classification and Properties.

statement: Give each building material an intersection priority from 0 to 999, adjustable by slider or list order, that decides which material prevails where elements intersect.
superiority: Priority matrix is visualised on the junction so users see why a skin passes through.

acceptance.sketch: Swap priorities 10 and 5 on two crossing walls and assert the pass-through material changes in the junction polygon.

notes: CORRECTED — range 0 to 999 and drag-to-reorder added. Read Intersection Priority (Building Material).

statement: List each skin of a composite or each fill of a profile as a component row with its building material, thickness and net or gross volume, so material quantities can be reported per skin and per building material.

source.ref: Element Listing Parameters > Component Data in Archicad

superiority: Multi-material split exact on curved elements.

acceptance.sketch: Sum over materials equals element volume.

notes: CORRECTED — reporting is done by component lists in the interactive schedule, one component per skin or profile fill. Read Component Data in Archicad.

statement: Define composites as ordered skins, up to 48, each with a building material, thickness, optional skin-end lines and a core, finish or other type, separated by lines with their own line type and pen.
superiority: Skins definable with formulas and parametric thickness.

acceptance.sketch: A composite of 0.04 + 0.10 + 0.20 m skins reports total thickness 0.34 m and refuses a 49th skin.

notes: CORRECTED — 48-skin limit, skin type core/finish/other and per-line type/pen documented. Read Composites, Edit and manage composites.

statement: Provide a composites dialog to insert, remove and reorder skins and separator lines with a live preview and a total-thickness readout.
superiority: Assembly editor shows live thermal values.

acceptance.sketch: Edit skin order updates model and drawing.

notes: VERIFIED — read Edit and manage composites; insert/remove skin, drag reorder, preview, total thickness shown.

statement: Draw complex profiles in a dedicated 2D profile editor from fills carrying a building material and cut-line type, and save them as named profiles selectable by walls, columns, beams, railings and some library parts.
superiority: Profile editor with constraints and parameters.

acceptance.sketch: Profile area equals polygon area.

notes: CORRECTED — profile editor window, per-tool 'use with' availability and only fills and hotspots saved. Read Profile Manager, Edit Complex Profile.

statement: Let a profile mark width and/or height stretch zones so a placed profiled wall, beam or column resizes with only the marked geometry stretching, reflected in nominal and total dimension parameters.
superiority: Profiles have named parameters and constraints, not only stretch zones.

acceptance.sketch: Resize host wall from 3 to 4 m: only the stretch zone grows by 1 m while fixed parts keep their exact size.

notes: CORRECTED — stretch modifiers support profiled walls, beams and columns only. Read Stretch Modifiers, Design Layers Panel.

statement: Define pen sets of 255 numbered pens with colour and weight, store, rename and delete custom sets, and apply one set to model views and a different one to the layout book or an individual drawing.

source.ref: Pen Sets > Edit and manage Pen Sets

superiority: Unlimited pens with named semantic roles.

acceptance.sketch: Switch pen set: all pens map to new colours consistently.

notes: CORRECTED — 255 pens confirmed; separate model/layout/drawing pen sets and Store As documented. Read Pen Sets, Apply Pen Set, Redefine Pen Set, Edit and manage Pen Sets.

statement: Keep a weight per pen in points or millimetres, shown true-to-weight on screen only when enabled and otherwise as hairlines, with a zero weight meaning the thinnest possible line and hairline output chosen at print time.

source.ref: Pen Sets > Edit and manage Pen Sets

superiority: Line weights verified from the PDF content stream.

acceptance.sketch: A 0.25 mm pen prints at 0.25 mm in the PDF within 0.01 mm.

notes: CORRECTED — weight shown only with True Line Weight; hairline is display-only, print has its own hairline switch. Read Edit and manage Pen Sets.

statement: Define zone categories as project attributes carrying a default background colour and a zone stamp object, assignable to each zone and recolouring plan and section cut zones.
superiority: Categories carry code requirements.

acceptance.sketch: Category assigned recolours plan fill.

notes: CORRECTED — a category holds colour and zone stamp only; no category code. Read Zone Categories.

statement: Define MEP systems as attributes limited to a single route type (duct, pipe or cable), carrying a fixed distribution-system class plus their own fills, lines and surfaces for plan, 3D and schematic display.

source.ref: MEP Systems and calculations > MEP Systems

superiority: Systems carry flow medium and sizing rules.

acceptance.sketch: System colour appears in 3D and plan.

notes: CORRECTED — building material is not listed; route type, distribution system and fill/line/surface display settings are. Available only with Collaborate or Max. Read MEP Systems.

statement: Define operation profiles as attributes holding an 8760-value hourly annual schedule for temperature band, occupant heat gain, domestic hot water and humidity loads, with DIN 18599 defaults, assignable per thermal block.
superiority: Same profile used for simulation.

acceptance.sketch: A profile holds 8760 hourly records; editing a daily schedule entry changes the annual totals by the expected amount.

notes: CORRECTED — 8760-hour daily-schedule structure and DIN 18599 default profiles documented. Read Operation Profiles (Energy Evaluation).

statement: Manage structural load cases grouped into load groups in a load manager and combine cases with factors in named load combinations that only store data for export, not run any calculation in the program.

source.ref: Structural Loads > Load Manager and Load Combination

superiority: Load model exchange with common structural solver formats through an open schema.

acceptance.sketch: Combination 1.35G+1.5Q yields load factors 1.35 and 1.5 on the right cases in the exported analytical model.

notes: CORRECTED — load groups and cases live in Load Manager (XML/SAF import, XML export); combinations carry factor and multiplier data. Read Load Manager, Load Combination Dialog Box.

statement: Define Markup Entry styles for Teamwork and BCF comments.
superiority: Style is tied to issue type and status, so BCF round trip maps to it.

acceptance.sketch: A markup entry created with style Clash shows its configured colour, and the style persists in the saved project.

notes: REJECTED: no markup-style attribute in Archicad 30 help; searched markup, markup style, markup entry. Issue handling documents issues and PDF markup, not a styled-entry attribute.

statement: Copy attributes between projects through an import dialog or a two-list attribute manager, matching incoming attributes by name or by index, optionally bringing associated attributes, with a changes list that can be reverted before closing.
superiority: Three-way merge with a diff report and per-attribute choice.

acceptance.sketch: Importing 3 same-named surfaces: By Name overwrites the existing ones, Append adds copies suffixed (1); Revert restores the prior set.

notes: CORRECTED — transfer commands Append / By Index / By Name documented; conflicts handled by overwrite or suffix (1), not a conflict-resolution wizard. Read Attribute Manager, Attribute Management Commands, Import attributes.

statement: Purge removes only attributes with zero references from a selection or folder, after listing them so the user can untick entries, and so can never create missing attributes.
superiority: Dry-run listing before purge and one-step undo.

acceptance.sketch: Purge removes exactly the attributes with zero references and none that are referenced, checked by reference count.

notes: CORRECTED — purge never replaces usage; replacement belongs to Delete and Replace. Read Purge attributes.

statement: Deleting an attribute that is in use opens a delete-and-replace step that substitutes a chosen replacement across elements and other attributes, with a warning and count of missing attributes if none is chosen.
superiority: Replacement can be scoped by query (storey, layer, classification).

acceptance.sketch: After replacing surface A by B across the model no element or library part references A.

notes: CORRECTED — substitution is offered through Delete and Replace for layers, lines, fills, surfaces, MEP systems, building materials, profiles and zone categories. Read Delete attributes.

statement: Provide read-only project templates that bundle project preferences, translator settings, tool default settings and placed elements, so every new project starts from the company standard.
superiority: Templates versioned and diffable.

acceptance.sketch: New file from template carries attributes.

notes: CORRECTED — template carries preferences, tool defaults and placed elements, with built-in and online templates. Read Template Files.

statement: Merge custom attributes defined by loaded library parts into the project attribute set without replacing same-name ones, with fills and lines merged from part scripts but surfaces and textures not merged.

source.ref: Attributes > Custom attributes of GDL objects

superiority: Resolution report with one-click remap to the nearest library item.

acceptance.sketch: Loading a library whose master script defines a fill named X while X exists keeps the existing X; a surface defined in a part script is not added.

notes: CORRECTED — help documents merge rules for master-script and part-script attributes; the 'mapping fixes for missing ones' wording is not documented. Read Custom attributes of GDL objects, Missing attributes.

statement: Offer named dimension standards that bundle unit, decimals and extra-accuracy settings per dimension type, storable from a custom setup and selectable from quick options, preferences or view settings.
superiority: Preset library per drafting standard (ISO, ANSI, national).

acceptance.sketch: A stored standard applied to the project sets unit and decimals for each of the 8 dimension types to the stored values.

notes: CORRECTED — 'marker styles' are not presets; documented are dimension standards with Store As. Read Dimensions Preferences.

statement: Define text styles with font, size, effects; missing font substitution.
superiority: Fonts are embedded in the PDF and project package, so output never changes by machine.

acceptance.sketch: Opening a project with a missing font substitutes it, logs the substitution and keeps text box extents within 2 percent.

notes: REJECTED: no named text-style attribute in Archicad 30 help; text formatting is via the formatting palette, text favorites and per-tool Text Style controls. Searched text style, fonts.

statement: Define working units for length, area, volume, angle, layout and unitless numbers used in dialogs and input, kept separate from dimension units and calculation units.
superiority: Mixed unit input accepted anywhere without loss.

acceptance.sketch: Converting a project from metres to feet leaves all geometry unchanged in physical size to 1e-9.

notes: CORRECTED — project origin and survey point are separate (Location Settings, Survey Point); working units are length/area/volume/angle/layout/unitless. Read Working Units.

statement: Define calculation units and decimals, with an extra-accuracy superscript option, and rules for computing values shown in interactive schedules, autotext labels and lists, separate from dimension units.
superiority: Calculation rules live in data and are selectable per country code.

acceptance.sketch: Zone area under the project rule rounds to the configured decimals, and the unrounded value stays available.

notes: CORRECTED — units/decimals/extra accuracy plus Setup Rules for schedule parameters. Read Calculation Units Preferences.

statement: Store the project location (latitude, longitude, time zone, altitude), project north and survey point in location settings, used by sun and energy analysis.
superiority: Georeferencing links project origin, survey point and CRS in one coordinate model.

acceptance.sketch: Sun position at the stored latitude, longitude and date matches an ephemeris value within 0.1 degree.

notes: CORRECTED — three panels: Project Location, Survey Point, Project North; 'project reference levels' belong to a separate Reference Levels preference. Read Location Settings.

statement: Define stories with name, elevation to project zero and height to the story above, inserting above or below, deleting and renaming, where changing a height shifts all stories above and changing an elevation moves one story only.
superiority: Level relationships are explicit constraints, rather than implicit offsets.

acceptance.sketch: Raising one story's height by 0.5 shifts every higher story by 0.5; changing one story's elevation alone changes the heights of its two neighbours only.

notes: VERIFIED — read Story Settings Dialog Box; height versus elevation semantics clarified in statement.

statement: Define grid systems, orthogonal or curved, with named grid lines, optional columns, objects or beams placed at intersections and automatic dimension lines.
superiority: Multiple named grid systems, each exportable as IFC grids.

acceptance.sketch: Two grid systems coexist; axes are labelled A to F and 1 to 6 and spacing equals input.

notes: CORRECTED — help documents orthogonal/curved geometry, elements at intersections, beams on gridlines, dimension lines; axis-label letters/numbers not read. Read Grid System Settings, Place a Grid System.

statement: Switch a view between entire model, without finishes, core only and load-bearing-core-only, driven by each component's structure type and saved per view.
superiority: Structure display is a per-view setting resolved at output.

acceptance.sketch: Core-only display removes finish skins and leaves the structural core volume unchanged; load-bearing option hides non-load-bearing and undefined elements.

notes: CORRECTED — it is a per-view display option, not an attribute; four options. Read Partial Structure Display.

statement: Let each door or window pick its dimension marker from predefined marker library objects or browse for another one, and toggle marker display on the plan.
superiority: Symbol sets are library data shared by team and imported by name.

acceptance.sketch: Switching the marker object of selected doors changes their plan markers consistently and leaves other doors untouched.

notes: CORRECTED — markers are library objects chosen per opening, not US/EU symbol sets. Read Other Panels in Door/Window Settings.

statement: Save tool settings, including dimensions, classification and property data, as named favorites kept in the project, applied from a palette, info box or settings dialog, and exchanged between projects by import and export.
superiority: Favourites can be shared through cloud libraries and templates.

acceptance.sketch: A stored favourite restores every field of the label settings exactly.

notes: CORRECTED — favorites store tool settings configurations with transfer sets choosing parameters; they are not limited to label and dimension settings. Read Favorites, Favorites Palette.

statement: Control IFC material handling in translator presets: on import use one default building material or create building materials named after IFC materials with optional mapping, and on export associate building material data with IFC materials.
superiority: Mapping is two-way and covered by the round-trip test corpus.

acceptance.sketch: An exported IFC file carries material names mapped from surfaces and building materials, and re-import restores the mapping.

notes: CORRECTED — mapping is a translator preset for import; export associates building materials to IFC materials in IFC4/4.3. Read Material and Surface Conversion, Data Conversion for IFC Export.

statement: Cost items and construction phases defined as attributes for scheduling.
superiority: Phases are first-class and drive quantities, cost and renovation views.

acceptance.sketch: Elements tagged phase 2 appear only under the matching phase filter and cost totals follow the phase.

notes: REJECTED: no cost or phase attribute type in Archicad 30 help; nearest are renovation status and renovation filters, which are views settings. Searched cost, phase, renovation.

statement: Keep a separate layer visibility and lock state for the layout book that affects only items placed directly on layouts, never the content of placed drawings, which follows the layers of their source view.

source.ref: Layers > Use separate layer settings for the Layout Book

superiority: Dino can show both layer contexts side by side and flag a drawing whose source layers differ from the layout state.

acceptance.sketch: Hiding a layer in the layout book hides a text placed on the layout but not the same-layer content inside a placed drawing.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Use separate layer settings for the Layout Book; layout-book layers act on directly placed items only.

statement: Provide a quick layers toolbar that hides, locks or unlocks the layers of the selected elements or of all other elements, toggles every layer's status, and undoes or redoes up to ten such actions.
superiority: Dino can extend quick layers to named scopes and keep a longer, persistent undo history.

acceptance.sketch: Selecting a wall and choosing hide others' layers hides all layers except the wall's; undo restores the previous statuses exactly.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Quick Layers; commands include hide/lock selection's layers, hide/lock others' layers, global toggles and ten-step undo.

statement: Let wall, beam and column profiles carry offset modifiers that shift individual profile edges per placed element, so one profile serves many variants, with modifier values usable in labels, schedules and expression properties.
superiority: Dino can allow offset modifiers on any extruded element and drive them from properties or formulas.

acceptance.sketch: Offsetting one edge of a profiled beam by 20 mm changes its cross-section area by edge length times 20 mm and leaves the profile attribute unchanged.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Offset Modifiers; available for wall, beam and column profiles and parametric modifiers are schedulable.

statement: Per profile component, set its core, finish or other type, an optional surface override, cut end lines, and whether its listed area is measured along a base line or base circle.
superiority: Dino can derive component area baselines automatically and show them as live overlays in the profile editor.

acceptance.sketch: A profile fill marked finish disappears under without-finishes display, and its listed component area equals base-line length times element length.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Components Panel; component type feeds partial structure display and area baseline feeds component schedules.

statement: Provide a built-in general surface that displays a solid colour taken from the element's uncut line pen and is the default for new building materials and surface parameters, so no attribute is ever left pointing at nothing.
superiority: Dino can make the fallback explicit and warn when many elements still use it.

acceptance.sketch: A new building material uses the general surface and renders in the pen colour of the element's uncut line.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Edit and manage surfaces; the general surface is hard coded and hidden from the surfaces dialog.

statement: Resolve surface texture images by file name ignoring extension and interpret name postfixes (colour, diffusion, bump, normal, alpha, specular, glow, displacement and others) as the channel each image feeds.
superiority: Dino can store the channel assignment explicitly instead of relying on name suffixes.

acceptance.sketch: A texture named wood_b and wood_n is assigned to the bump and normal channels respectively; changing the extension does not break the link.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Texture files - naming conventions; postfix list with combined forms such as cs.

statement: Display fills on screen either in true appearance or as a stored bitmap pattern per fill, while print and plot always use the true appearance.

source.ref: Fills > Fill Display Mode: True Fill Appearance vs. Bitmap

superiority: Dino can generate the bitmap pattern automatically from the true fill so it never goes stale.

acceptance.sketch: With true-fill display off, plan fills draw as the stored bitmaps, and the exported PDF still contains the vector pattern.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Fill Display Mode; on-screen option only, output unaffected, bitmaps must be edited manually when a fill changes.

statement: Restrict each composite to chosen element types (wall, slab, roof, shell) so that composite choosers list only composites whose use-with flags include the element type.

source.ref: Composites > Edit and manage composites (Use With)

superiority: Dino can show filtered-out composites greyed with the reason instead of hiding them.

acceptance.sketch: A composite flagged for roof and shell only is absent from the wall composite chooser and present in the shell chooser.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Edit and manage composites and Assign composite to wall, slab, roof or shell; use-with icons filter the pop-ups.

statement: Show all pending attribute changes in a changes list while the attribute manager is open, let the user revert selected or all of them, or apply them all without closing.

source.ref: Attribute Manager > Revert Changes in Attribute Manager

superiority: Dino can keep the change list across sessions as an auditable attribute change log.

acceptance.sketch: After deleting two surfaces and renaming a pen set, reverting the two deletions restores them and leaves the rename pending.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Revert Changes in Attribute Manager; Revert and Apply All act until the dialog closes.

statement: When elements are pasted or hotlinked from another project, map incoming attributes by name: add unknown names keeping their index when free, reuse same-name attributes when definitions agree, and create suffixed copies for conflicting profiles and layers.

source.ref: Attributes > Handling of attributes during paste and hotlink

superiority: Dino can preview the attribute mapping before paste and let the user redirect conflicts.

acceptance.sketch: Pasting an element whose profile has the host profile's name but a different shape creates a profile named with suffix (1) and leaves the host profile untouched.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Handling of attributes during paste and hotlink; rules differ per attribute type and folders do not transfer.

statement: Save a single pen set in the AutoCAD plot style table format so each colour maps to a line width on plots made elsewhere.

source.ref: Pen Sets > Save Pen Set in STB Format

superiority: Dino can also read STB tables to create pen sets, making the exchange round-trip.

acceptance.sketch: Saving a pen set to STB and reading the file back yields 255 entries with the same weights to 0.01 mm.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Save Pen Set in STB Format; export of one selected pen set only is documented.

statement: Find and select elements that refer to missing attributes by combining an element-type criterion with an attributes-missing criterion, so broken references can be located and reassigned.

source.ref: Missing attributes > Find and Select elements with missing attributes

superiority: Dino can list missing references with their element and attribute name and offer one-click replacement.

acceptance.sketch: A slab whose cover fill was deleted without replacement is selected by the missing-attributes criterion and no intact slab is.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Find and Select elements with missing attributes and Missing attributes; causes include paste, library parts and deletion.
